title: AI-mediated information and fragmented institutional responsibility are turning uncertainty itself into a democratic risk
source_unit: Full Fact, Full Fact Report 2026: A system under strain—strengthening the UK's democratic information environment
geography: United Kingdom, with international comparisons and lessons for democratic information resilience

observations.period: 2026; misinformation concern, trust and democratic participation

denominator.unit: Full Fact UK public polling and report synthesis; individual polling denominators vary by question

political_misinformation_concern.unit: percent of UK adults expressing concern about political misinformation

political_institution_trust_damage.unit: percent of the concerned group saying concern about misinformation negatively affected trust in political institutions over the past year

mainstream_media_trust_damage.unit: percent of the concerned group saying concern about misinformation negatively affected trust in mainstream-media accuracy

youth_online_political_information.unit: percent of UK 13-17-year-olds reporting exposure to political information online

youth_confident_assessing_truth.unit: percent of UK 13-17-year-olds confident they can tell whether online political information is true or false

peer_truth_assessment_confidence.unit: percent of UK 13-17-year-olds confident that other people their age can assess whether online political information is true or false

observations.method: Full Fact report drawing on its own polling, fact-checking and case analysis, public research, interviews, policy review, and international evidence; the report is an advocacy and policy analysis rather than a single probability-sample survey.
observations.uncertainty: Polling questions have different samples and fieldwork details; reported associations do not establish that misinformation caused trust or participation changes, and Full Fact’s institutional perspective shapes the policy diagnosis.
observations.subgroup: UK adults, adults concerned about political misinformation, young people aged 13-17, voters, journalists, fact checkers, public authorities, platforms and AI-mediated information users.
observations.counterinterpretation: Scepticism can strengthen democratic scrutiny; the report distinguishes healthy skepticism from corrosive cynicism and does not imply that all disagreement or uncertainty is misinformation.

observations.period: 2026; AI-mediated search, platform design and institutional readiness

denominator.unit: Full Fact information-environment assessment and cited UK evidence

ai_answer_exposure.unit: percent of people in the UK regularly seeing an AI-generated answer to one of their searches in the past week in cited 2025 evidence

institutional_gap.value: no single institution is responsible for system-wide coherence of the UK democratic information environment

risk_pathway.value: AI summaries, synthetic media, recommender systems, monetised incentives, reduced moderation and fragmented public responsibility can weaken authoritative signals and increase uncertainty

policy_response.value: four mutually reinforcing reform pillars: secure the information ecosystem, strengthen public resilience, modernise laws and institutions, and increase commercial transparency and accountability

observations.method: Full Fact systems analysis of information flows during elections and crises, platform and AI mediation, UK legal and institutional arrangements, and international governance examples.
observations.uncertainty: The report is a policy diagnosis and does not provide a causal estimate of how much any single platform, AI tool or regulatory gap changes electoral outcomes or public trust.
observations.subgroup: People receiving information through search, social platforms, chatbots and recommendation systems; public-interest media; regulators; election authorities; crisis communicators; and platform operators.
observations.counterinterpretation: Automated tools can improve accessibility and speed, and platform or AI reforms may produce trade-offs involving expression, privacy, competition, and institutional overreach.

related_sources.claim: Canonical Full Fact report page and executive summary.
Official 105-page report PDF with methods, cases, international lessons and recommendations.

boundary: This record adds a UK democratic-information route connecting platform design, AI mediation, synthetic media, institutional coordination, media literacy, trust and participation. It is a policy and advocacy report with cited polling and cases, not a representative global prevalence estimate, an algorithm audit, a causal electoral study, or respondent-level raw-data ingestion.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official Full Fact landing page and 105-page PDF were reviewed; report scope, executive-summary diagnosis, UK polling figures, AI-search exposure, institutional fragmentation and four reform pillars were cross-checked.
